principle_violations.reason: The PaymentProcessor interface enforces all implementing classes to provide the `auth_sms` method, even if it's not applicable to all types of payment processors (e.g., PaypalPaymentProcessor).
principle_violations.suggestion: Split the PaymentProcessor interface into smaller, more specific interfaces that only define the methods relevant to their domain. Classes can then implement only the interfaces they need.

original_code: public abstract class PaymentProcessor { public abstract void pay(Order order);  public abstract void auth_sms(Order order, String code); }

public class PaypalPaymentProcessor extends PaymentProcessor { @Override public void pay(Order order) {System.out.println("Processing paypal payment...");} @Override public void auth_sms(Order order, String securityCode) { throw new UnsupportedOperationException(); }}
suggestion_code: public interface BasicPaymentProcessor { void pay(Order order); } public interface SMSAuthenticatable { void authSMS(Order order, String code); }
public class PaypalPaymentProcessor implements BasicPaymentProcessor { public void pay(Order order) { System.out.println("Processing PayPal Payment..."); }}
